source.title: Expected Gradients of Maxout Networks and Consequences to Parameter Initialization

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and evaluates a maxout initialization strategy, comparing training outcomes across initializations. It reports test accuracy and convergence behavior, rather than the training classification error named by the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-set accuracy, not training classification error. It also states that some initializations make training fail to progress, but supplies no numerical training-error results. The reported accuracy rows are included only as evidence on initialization and training behavior; they cannot establish near-zero training error.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 in a new activation setting: plain maxout networks. It compares initialization schemes, explicitly reports faster convergence and failures to start training, and measures gradient stability across depth. V4 does not require training classification error; the record incorrectly applies V1's measurement requirement to V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors derive activation-specific Gaussian initialization guidelines for wide fully connected maxout networks and empirically report improved SGD and Adam training in deep fully connected networks and CNNs. They report better or comparable test accuracy to the tested ReLU networks. CNN gradient theory remains unproved, and input dependence complicates universal gradient stabilization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives and tests an initialization strategy for maxout networks, comparing it with other maxout initializations and ReLU-He. It reports test accuracy and qualitative training progress, not training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization constant c and initialization scheme affect reported test accuracy and whether training progresses; optimizer and dataset are also varied.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix J.4 compares wider or deeper ReLU networks with maxout networks using test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and parameter allocation affect final generalization performance; these comparisons do not establish the training-error degradation or shortcut effect in V3.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2023; PMLR 202, 2023)
record.problems: Training classification error is not reported; reported classification metric is test accuracy. Training experiments are averaged over 4 runs. Some table entries show large variability, including 50.83±40.83 for CIFAR-10 at c = 0.7 in Table 10.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2, 3 and 10 contain many additional initialization and dataset rows; retained the CIFAR-10/100 results that show the proposed initialization, He comparison, early Adam convergence, and notable initialization sensitivity. Other datasets and routine initialization constants are omitted. The tables report test accuracy, not training error.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error and corrupted or random labels.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs and its prevention by identity shortcuts.
Orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization, 10,000-layer convolutional training, and a controlled training experiment sweeping depth to establish maximum trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Same-network comparisons of normalization versus no normalization for speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Uniform maxout Adam results were replaced by the adjacent max-pooling column. Add CIFAR-10 accuracies 87.31±0.51, 87.96±0.75 and 91.06±0.22, and CIFAR-100 accuracies 53.43±1.08, 57.65±0.75 and 61.96±0.58 at 100, 200 and 1000 epochs. Add corresponding early He comparisons.

Gradient-versus-depth experiments show stable gradients for width-50 fully connected and convolutional maxout networks at c=0.55555, compared with other variance choices. Record the width, depth, input dependence and gradient measure; this directly checks the proposed mechanism.

During MNIST training, gradients for c=2 and c=10 explode to NaN; plotted alternatives remain stable after an initial increase. This directly records training instability absent from the accuracy rows.

Initialization sensitivity persists with batch normalization: at c=1e-6 and 1e-5 accuracy is at chance, while c=0.55555 gives CIFAR-10 77.68±1.07 and CIFAR-100 42±1.51. These networks are narrower and use fixed learning rate 0.01, so they cannot serve as a normalization-versus-no-normalization comparison.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. Poor results under mismatched initialization support initialization sensitivity; they do not warrant limits_scope for V4. Table 3 columns were systematically confused. Endpoint test accuracy provides supporting context but does not independently measure optimization speed.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, is not reported.
No teacher-student two-layer ReLU local-minimum experiment.
No comparison of plain and residual networks for the claimed depth effect.

The paper studies maxout initialization, not the listed initialization methods for plain tanh networks or 10,000-layer convolutional networks. It does not measure training classification error or compare Gaussian and orthogonal weights.
No learning-rate stability-threshold or catapult experiment.
Batch normalization is not the focus of the comparisons; no same-network normalization speed or learning-rate-tolerance test.

relation.reason: Its own theoretical and experimental comparisons directly examine how initialization affects gradient stability and training in deep networks.

tranche.reason: The study extends activation-matched initialization to plain deep maxout networks and reports gradient stability, training success and faster convergence, testing V4 in a new activation setting.

source_check.notes: The row notes incorrectly describe V4 as a training-classification-error claim; V4 concerns learning speed and trainable depth. Reported uncertainties are standard deviations across four runs; the initialization theory covers fully connected networks, with CNN applicability supported experimentally.

reader_labels.reason: Some tested initializations have markedly lower test accuracy, and the authors say performance can be worse or training can fail to progress; rows R2, R4, R8, R12–R18.
